stem:
Kadoma Ceramics Ltd makes tiles and pottery. On 1 November 2025 it issued 70,000 ordinary shares of US\$1 each at US\$1.55, and all the proceeds were received in cash during the year. The trial balance below was extracted at 30 June 2026, the end of the financial year, after the share issue.

**Kadoma Ceramics Ltd: trial balance at 30 June 2026**

| Account | Debit US\$ | Credit US\$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Inventory at 1 July 2025 | 43,700 |  |
| Purchases | 322,600 |  |
| Sales |  | 531,000 |
| Distribution expenses | 38,900 |  |
| Administrative expenses | 75,300 |  |
| Loan note interest paid | 3,200 |  |
| Interim dividend paid | 12,600 |  |
| Land and buildings at cost | 248,000 |  |
| Equipment at cost | 262,000 |  |
| Accumulated depreciation of equipment |  | 70,500 |
| Trade receivables | 57,400 |  |
| Bank | 64,300 |  |
| Trade payables |  | 42,300 |
| Ordinary shares of US\$1 each |  | 310,000 |
| Share premium |  | 46,000 |
| 10% loan notes |  | 64,000 |
| Retained earnings at 1 July 2025 |  | 64,200 |
| **Total** | **1,128,000** | **1,128,000** |

**Information at 30 June 2026**

| No. | Information |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Inventory at 30 June 2026 was valued at US\$47,900. |
| 2 | Equipment is depreciated at 15% of its cost. Land and buildings are not depreciated. |
| 3 | Loan note interest for the second half of the year, US\$3,200, was owing. |
| 4 | The income tax charge for the year is estimated at US\$14,800. |
| 5 | A final dividend of US\$9,500 was declared before the year end and remains unpaid. |

Give percentages to one decimal place.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: For the share issue on 1 November 2025, calculate:

parts.label: (i)

parts.label: (ii)

parts.stem: profit from operations
parts.explanation: Gross profit 212,600 - distribution 38,900 - administrative expenses 114,600 (including depreciation 39,300) = US\$59,100.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Gross profit 212,600 - distribution 38,900 - administrative expenses 114,600 (including depreciation 39,300) = US\$59,100.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.stem: profit for the year
parts.explanation: 59,100 - finance costs 6,400 - tax 14,800 = US\$37,900. Finance costs are interest paid 3,200 plus the accrual 3,200.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 59,100 - finance costs 6,400 - tax 14,800 = US\$37,900. Finance costs are interest paid 3,200 plus the accrual 3,200.

Revenue 531,000, cost of sales 318,400 and gross profit 212,600
Distribution costs 38,900 and administrative expenses 114,600, giving profit from operations 59,100
Finance costs 6,400, profit before tax 52,700, income tax 14,800 and profit for the year 37,900

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Calculate gearing at 30 June 2026, using the Cambridge formula.
hints: Capital employed = shares + all reserves + non-current liabilities.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: State two reasons why the directors may have preferred to issue shares instead of raising the money by borrowing.

points.description: No fixed interest has to be paid and there is no repayment date
Gearing stays lower, so the financial risk is smaller

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A share issue carries no compulsory interest or repayment, and keeps gearing lower than more borrowing would.

parts.explanation: One mark for each valid reason.

explanation: This Cambridge Paper 2 style question asks for the share issue, the statement of profit or loss, the statement of financial position and gearing for a company.
hints: The trial balance is after the share issue.
Finance costs include the accrued interest.
Retained earnings are reduced by both dividends.

stem: Bulawayo Textiles Ltd has 540,000 ordinary shares of US\$1 each, share premium of US\$62,000 and retained earnings of US\$238,000. On 1 September 2025 it made a rights issue of one new share for every four held at US\$1.65 per share. All the rights were taken up and the money was received on the same day.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the number of new shares issued.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the cash received.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the amount credited to the share premium account.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate total equity after the issue.
parts.explanation: Total equity before = 540,000 + 62,000 + 238,000 = 840,000; plus the cash raised 222,750 = US\$1,062,750.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Total equity before = 540,000 + 62,000 + 238,000 = 840,000; plus the cash raised 222,750 = US\$1,062,750.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Prepare the bank account entry and the share capital and share premium accounts for the rights issue.

points.description: Bank: debit 222,750 (rights money received)
Ordinary share capital: credit 135,000
Share premium: credit 87,750
Each entry dated, with a clear description and the totals agreeing

answerSpec.markingNotes:
Example answer: **Bank account (rights issue)**

| Date | Details | US\$ | Date | Details | US\$ |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| 1 Sep | Ordinary share capital and share premium | 222,750 |  |  |  |

**Ordinary share capital account**

| Date | Details | US\$ | Date | Details | US\$ |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
|  |  |  | 1 Sep | Bank: rights issue of 135,000 shares at US\$1 | 135,000 |

**Share premium account**

| Date | Details | US\$ | Date | Details | US\$ |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
|  |  |  | 1 Sep | Bank: 135,000 shares × US\$0.65 | 87,750 |

parts.explanation: One mark for each account and one for clear descriptions that agree.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Explain two benefits to the company of making a rights issue instead of a public issue of shares.

points.description: It is cheaper to arrange, since it is offered to existing shareholders who already know the company
Control stays with the present shareholders in proportion to their holdings
The shareholders have the first right to buy, so the shares are likely to be taken up and the cash is raised quickly

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A rights issue costs less than a public issue, existing shareholders keep their share of control, and because it is offered to those who know the company it is likely to be taken up.

parts.explanation: One mark for each benefit, up to three.

explanation: This Cambridge Paper 2 style question covers the calculations, ledger entries and benefits of a rights issue.
hints: The premium per share is the issue price less US\$1.

stem:
Mutoko Mining Supplies Ltd sells tools and protective clothing to small mines. Extracts from its financial statements for the years 2024 and 2025 are shown. Use year-end figures, give percentages to one decimal place and ratios to two decimal places.

| Item | 2024 US\$ | 2025 US\$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Revenue | 438,000 | 489,000 |
| Gross profit | 157,680 | 158,925 |
| Profit from operations | 74,580 | 67,725 |
| Capital employed | 293,700 | 347,400 |
| Inventory | 41,700 | 63,200 |
| Trade receivables | 33,900 | 52,300 |
| Cash and cash equivalents | 19,400 | 3,200 |
| Current liabilities | 37,300 | 59,300 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the gross profit margin for:

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate return on capital employed (ROCE) for:

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the current ratio for:

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the acid test ratio for:

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: A bank has been asked to lend the company a further US\$40,000. Evaluate the profitability and liquidity of the company and advise the bank.

points.description: Profitability has fallen: gross margin from 36.0% to 32.5% and ROCE from 25.4% to 19.5%
Revenue grew by 11.6%, so growth has not brought more profit
Liquidity has weakened: current ratio 2.55 to 2.00 and acid test 1.43 to 0.94
Cash is only US\$3,200 while inventory and receivables have risen sharply (overtrading)
Judgement and recommendation: lend only with security and a plan to improve the margin and collect receivables, or decline

answerSpec.modelAnswer: The company is growing but less profitable: the gross margin and ROCE have fallen. Liquidity is weaker, cash is very low and inventory and receivables have grown, which suggests overtrading. The bank should lend only against security and a clear plan to restore the margin and collect receivables.

parts.explanation: One mark for each point, up to five; allow follow-through from the calculations.

explanation: This Cambridge Paper 2 style question asks for profitability and liquidity ratios and an evaluation for a lender.
hints: Remove inventory for the acid test.
